guideTitle: 6 Best Large Non Slip Shower Mats in 2026
metaTitle: Best Large Non Slip Shower Mats in 2026
metaDescription: Six extra large shower stall mats from 47 to 58 inches compared by suction cups, drain design, trim-to-fit options and material for walk-in shower floors.
introParagraphs: A walk-in shower floor is a different space from a tub: it is wider, usually roughly square, often with a drain in the middle or the corner and no raised wall at the ends to keep a mat from sliding. A small tub mat leaves most of that floor bare. A large shower mat, typically around 47 by 32 inches or bigger, covers the walking area so that every step lands on grip.

The six mats here are the MARIBUR 47.2 by 31.5 inch loofah-style mat with a central drain hole, the Yonala 47.2 by 31.5 inch TPE mat with 330-plus suction cups and 442 drain holes, the Yolife 47 by 32 inch TPE mat with 330 cups, the Tiamo 47 by 32 inch TPE mat with 600-plus drain holes, the ZAPPUP 58 by 44 inch loofah mat and the Yonala PVC loofah mat that trims to fit.

We evaluated each on size, how it stays put, drainage around the drain, material and cleaning. Large mats raise their own problems: they hold more water, curl at the edges and are heavier to lift, so the details of drainage and trimming matter as much as the headline dimensions. Always measure your floor and the drain position before ordering.

products.name: Yonala Extra Large Shower Mat, 47.2 x 31.5 Inch, TPE With Suction Cups
products.description:
Yonala's TPE mat states the numbers that matter on a large mat: more than 330 suction cups for grip across a big floor and 442 optimized drainage holes to prevent pooling. At 47.2 by 31.5 inches it fits most walk-in showers, tubs and shower stalls, according to the listing, and it has a hole for the drain in the middle. TPE is soft and comfortable on bare feet.

On a large mat, the cups have to hold a lot of area, and a count above 330 spreads the hold. The 442 holes help water reach the drain instead of pooling, which matters because large mats hold more water and take longer to dry. As with all suction mats, the floor must be smooth and non-porous.

Compared with the Yolife it states a drain hole count, and compared with the loofah mats it grips with suction. It suits a smooth walk-in shower floor with a central drain where a cup-based, quick-draining mat is wanted. If your shower has a curb at the entrance, check that the mat clears it so that it does not catch a foot when you step in.
products.bestFor: A smooth walk-in shower with a central drain.
pros: 330+ suction cups across a large mat
cons: Large mat is heavy to lift and wash
Drain position must match your floor

products.name: Tiamo Extra Large Shower Mat, 47x32 Inch, 100% TPE, 600+ Drain Holes
specs: Sticks to the wall for storage
products.description:
Tiamo sells a rectangle of 100 percent TPE rather than PVC, with more than 600 large drain holes that the listing says give 30 percent faster water run-off, plus over 330 suction cups. The 47 by 32 inch mat has a clever storage feature: its suction cups let it stick to the shower wall after use, so it hangs and dries instead of lying on the floor. The listing says the mat rinses clean in seconds.

Drying a big mat is the chore people skip, and hanging it on the wall is the simplest way to make sure it dries. A high hole count helps water flow through. TPE is soft, odorless and flexible, and a big TPE sheet is lighter than a thick PVC one, which makes the mat easier to lift.

Compared with the Yonala it has more holes and the wall-storage idea, and compared with the ZAPPUP it is a suction mat in TPE. It suits a household that wants the mat to dry between uses without effort. Hang it from the wall as soon as you finish rinsing, and the mat will usually be dry by the next shower.
products.bestFor: A big mat that hangs on the wall to dry.
pros: Cups let the mat stick to the wall to dry
cons: Needs a smooth floor and a smooth wall
Large mat still takes effort to lift

products.name: Yolife Large Shower Mat, 47 x 32 Inch, Soft TPE, 330 Suction Cups
products.description:
Yolife's mat is the straightforward version of the large TPE idea: 47 by 32 inches, a textured surface, 330 powerful suction cups that the listing says adhere nicely to a smooth shower floor and larger, denser drain holes. The material is a soft, no-odor TPE. It has a central drain hole for a typical stall.

The virtue here is simplicity: a stated cup count, a stated size and a soft material. The listing describes the drainage in general terms and gives no hole count in the text we have. Like the other cup-based mats, it needs a smooth, non-porous floor.

Compared with the Yonala it gives no hole count, and compared with the Tiamo it has no storage trick. It suits a buyer who wants a plain, large, cup-based mat without extras. If the central hole does not line up with your drain, trim a small opening instead of moving the whole mat.
products.bestFor: A plain, large TPE mat with a stated cup count.
cons: Drain hole count is not stated in the text we have

products.name: MARIBUR Extra Large Non Slip Shower Mat, 47.2 x 31.5 Inch, Loofah
products.description:
MARIBUR takes the other route on a large mat: no suction cups, but a lattice-textured non-slip backing the listing says will not damage a shower floor, topped by a soft, loofah-like surface 0.4 inch thick. The mat is 47.2 by 31.5 inches with a drain hole in the middle. The listing contrasts it with suction mats that are hard to clean and prone to slipping.

A thick loofah top is cushioned and gentle, and without cups there is nothing to scrub grime from, which makes cleaning simpler. The trade is that grip depends on the backing's friction rather than a seal, so it may slide more on a very smooth floor. The listing does not give a weight figure in the text we have.

Compared with the Yonala it has no cups, and compared with the ZAPPUP it is smaller. It suits a shower floor where cups do not seal, or a buyer who wants a thick, soft mat. Because foam wears, expect to replace it every year or two, and keep the receipt for the size.
products.bestFor: A thick, soft mat on a floor where cups do not seal.
pros: No suction cups, lattice backing grips
cons: Friction grip may slide on a very smooth floor
Weight is not stated in the text we have

products.name: Yonala Extra Large Shower Mat, 47.2 x 31.5 Inch, PVC Loofah, Trim-to-Fit
products.description:
This Yonala is the cut-it-yourself version: an oversized PVC loofah mat of 47.2 by 31.5 inches that the listing says can be cut to any shape, with a strong grip bottom said to give elderly users and kids solid footing and an open weave that drains water straight through. The point of trimming is to fill an irregular shower floor without gaps or overhang.

Shower floors are often not rectangles: a corner drain, a curved edge or a bench can all leave a standard mat poorly fitted. A trimmable mat solves that, and an open weave dries quickly. Cutting is permanent, so measure and cut conservatively. The listing's grip claims are the maker's.

Compared with the Yonala TPE it has no cups and can be cut, and compared with the MARIBUR it adds trimming as a headline feature. It suits an irregular shower floor that needs a custom fit. Mark the cut lines with a pen first, and cut a little outside them so that you can fine-tune.
products.bestFor: Irregular shower floors that need a custom shape.
pros: Can be trimmed to any shape
Open weave drains and dries quickly
cons: Grip is by friction, not suction

products.name: ZAPPUP Extra Large Shower Mat, 58 x 44 Inch, Non Slip Loofah
products.description:
ZAPPUP offers the biggest mat in the guide at 58 by 44 inches, made of PVC with grid-shaped anti-slip particles on the bottom and a porous, hollow loofah structure that forms drainage channels for quick drainage and drying. The listing says the larger size is more suitable for a shower room. At that scale it can cover an entire wet-room or large walk-in floor.

Such a large mat is a floor treatment more than a mat, and it will usually need trimming to fit around a drain or a bench. A porous structure helps it drain and dry, though a big sheet still takes time to dry. The listing gives no thickness or weight in the text we have.

Compared with the 47-inch mats it covers far more floor, and compared with the trimmable Yonala it is larger. It suits a large walk-in shower or wet room where the whole floor should be covered. If you cut it into sections, you can use the offcuts as small mats by the sink or toilet.
products.bestFor: Large walk-in showers and wet-room floors.
pros: 58 by 44 in covers a large floor
Porous hollow structure drains and dries
cons: Thickness and weight are not stated in the text we have

buyingCriteria.criterion: Measure the floor and the drain
buyingCriteria.explanation: A large mat only helps if it fits the floor, and a shower floor is rarely a clean rectangle. Measure the length and width, and mark where the drain sits. The Yonala and Yolife list a central drain hole, and the loofah mats can be trimmed. A mat that covers the drain pools water.

The Yonala TPE, Yolife and Tiamo mats list 330 or more suction cups, while the MARIBUR, ZAPPUP and trimmable Yonala use a textured backing. Cups need a smooth, non-porous floor, and a patterned backing relies on friction. Match the mechanism to your floor and test with a firm foot shove. This test is simple: place the mat dry, push it with a foot and repeat when wet, which shows how much hold it really has.

A large mat holds a lot of water. The Yonala lists 442 holes, the Tiamo 600 or more and the loofah mats use porous structures. Water that cannot reach the drain lifts and floats the mat and breeds mildew. Choose strong drainage and lift the mat after each shower.

TPE on the Yonala, Yolife and Tiamo is soft and relatively light, and thick PVC loofah on the MARIBUR and ZAPPUP is cushioned but heavier when wet. A big mat is a chore to lift, so weight matters. Consider who will lift and rinse it. If you are unsure, hold a corner of the mat and feel how much it weighs, since the weight of a wet mat is several times that of a dry one.

The Tiamo's cups let it stick to the wall to dry, which is a clever solution to a big, wet mat. Others can be hung over a rail or draped over the shower door. Drying prevents mildew. Plan a place for it. Look at the way the mat is made at the edges, since a thin edge curls and a thick one stays flat.

The trimmable Yonala can be cut to shape, and others can be trimmed too if the material allows. Edges that run up a wall or over a bench curl and trip. Cut slowly and round the corners. Measure twice. Think about where the drain sits and whether the mat should have a hole there or be trimmed around it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Coverage and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared sizes from 47 by 32 inches to 58 by 44 inches, and the option to trim. We considered drain position and floor shape. Coverage that fits earned the most credit. Large mats raise issues that small ones do not, so we weighed drain position, drying and weight heavily.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip mechanism
howWeEvaluated.description: Suction counts above 330 and patterned backings were compared. We noted surface requirements. Stated numbers and honest limits earned credit. We compared the numbers that listings give, and noted where they stay silent about thickness or weight.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drainage and drying
howWeEvaluated.description: Hole counts, such as 442 on the Yonala and 600-plus on the Tiamo, and porous structures were compared. We favored the wall-storage idea on the Tiamo for drying. The wall-hanging idea on the Tiamo was credited because drying is the weak point of any large mat.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: TPE, PVC and loofah foams were compared for softness and weight. We considered the effort of lifting a wet mat. Lighter, softer materials scored higher. We considered how easy it is to fit a mat to an irregular floor, which is common in walk-in showers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Edge and fit behavior
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how each mat will lie around drains, benches and walls and whether it can be trimmed. Edges that curl were treated as a hazard. We aimed to judge how each mat would behave after months of use, when foam and cups both age.

howToChoose.note: Measure the floor and drain twice before ordering.

faq.q: What size should a large shower mat be?
faq.a: It should fill the walking area without climbing walls or covering the drain. The mats here run from 47 by 32 inches to 58 by 44 inches. Measure your floor and the drain position first. Many people place a large mat so that it overlaps the drain slightly and then trim the overlap, which is easier than trying to align a cut-out.

faq.q: Can I cut a large shower mat?
faq.a: Some can, such as the trimmable Yonala PVC loofah mat. Check the listing first, cut slowly with sharp scissors and round the corners. Cutting is permanent. A large mat keeps the whole floor grippy, but it also hides standing water, so lift and dry it often.

faq.q: Suction cups or no cups on a big mat?
faq.a: Cups hold strongly on a smooth floor, as on the Yonala TPE with 330-plus cups. A patterned backing, as on the MARIBUR, suits textured floors and avoids cups to clean. Choose by your floor. If the shower has a bench or seat, trim the mat to leave a clear edge so that the leg of the bench does not sit on it.

faq.q: How do I dry a big mat?
faq.a: Lift it after each shower and hang it. The Tiamo's cups let it stick to the wall to dry. Drying prevents mildew. A brush with warm soapy water removes the film that collects on a big textured mat and keeps the surface grippy.

faq.q: Will a large mat cover my drain?
faq.a: It can, which makes water pool. The Yonala and Yolife have a central drain hole, and others can be trimmed. Check the drain position before ordering. If you rent, a large suction mat leaves no marks, while a trimmed mat is a permanent change to the mat only.

faq.q: Is a large mat safe for an older adult?
faq.a: It can help by giving a grippy surface across the whole floor, but edges that curl are a trip hazard. Press the edges flat and add a grab bar. A therapist can advise. Replace any mat that curls or loses its grip, because a big mat that lifts at the edge is a hazard.
